ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Figure A shows a fixed closed rectangular coil abcd, with a and b on the left, d and c on the right, and black dots around and inside the coil indicating a uniform magnetic field, whose direction is perpendicular to the paper surface outward. Figure B is the curve of magnetic induction intensity B varying with time t: B begins to increase from t=0, reaches the highest point at t=2 s, and a vertical dashed line in the figure marks t=2 s; afterward B decreases, and becomes 0 at t=4 s. Reasoning: The coil is fixed, so the coil area S remains unchanged, and the magnetic flux through the coil is Φ=BS. At t=2 s, the B-t curve is at the highest point, and the instantaneous slope is 0, that is, dB/dt=0. Therefore dΦ/dt=S·dB/dt=0, the induced electromotive force is 0, and the induced current I in the closed coil is 0. The magnitude of the Ampere force on side ab satisfies F=BIL; although B is not 0 at this time, I=0, so F=0. Final answer: At t=2 s, the Ampere force on side ab is 0.
